title: Sealed: the random beacon (a control that must fail)

data.source: NIST Randomness Beacon, version 2.0, the pulse at 12:00 UTC on each day from 10 September to 18 November 2026

claim_kind: prediction (sealed before the event; not yet scored)
prediction: A control. The seed (q = 0.9) forecasts each of 120 noon numbers from the ones before it; its first forecast is 0.48. The scoring rule must NOT print fits.
baseline: Rules fixed the same night: persistence, the mean of the last 50, the field's rule (always 0.5: the beacon is built to be uniform and unpredictable) and a decoy. On the second half of the stored table their mean misses were crr 0.252, field 0.239, running mean 0.242, persistence 0.327, decoy 0.239.
status_line: A sealed envelope. Opens on or after 31 March 2027.
why: The event has not happened, so nothing could be scored tonight. The envelope is sealed (seal 506d9d2ddbec...) and will be scored by its own frozen rule when it opens.
